Definition: from G303 and G3982; to incite:--persuade.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in the charge against Paul at Corinth: 'This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.' It is inciting, stirring up — the accusers say Paul is talking people into a worship the law forbids, and Gallio throws the case out.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for persuading carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the charge — Paul persuading men to worship God, and the charge itself proving the gospel was spreading.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
